ann_25.original: Hidden node 773 is the model's veto on too few first values. It reads the count of attributes that take their first value (a1 = 1, a2 = 1, a3 = 1, a4 = 1, a5 = 1, a6 = 1): each of the six first-value indicators enters it with a negative weight (see the formula), so the node falls as the count rises, and its large negative output weight then pushes the prediction to no. On the training split the veto is on for 89 of the 89 rows with a count below two (share 100%), and on for 0 of the 143 rows with a count of three or more. For the count-below-two rows its mean contribution to the score through this part is -58.6 logits, against 15.9 from the direct edges, so the model's mean predicted probability there is 1.7e-07 (training outcome rate 0%). This is the at-least-two side of the MONK-2 concept.
